sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *antes de* and *después de* + infinitive from A2 Unit 4, and *cuando* + subjunctive for the future from A2 Unit 27. They are the tools for telling a story in order, and the Popol Vuh is a story of things done one after another: the gods try clay, then wood, then maize. When the same person does both actions, the infinitive does not change.

sections.title: Putting events in order
rows: Antes de crear a los humanos, los dioses hicieron animales.
*antes de* + infinitive: before creating humans, the gods made animals
Después de probar con barro, probaron con madera.
*después de* + infinitive: after trying clay, they tried wood
Después de vencer a los señores, los gemelos subieron al cielo.
*después de* + infinitive: after defeating the lords, the twins went up
Cuando llegue la lluvia, las familias sembrarán el maíz.
*cuando* + subjunctive for a future time: when the rain comes, the families will plant maize

items.spanish: Antes de subir al cielo, los gemelos vencieron a los señores de Xibalbá.
items.english: Before going up to the sky, the twins defeated the lords of Xibalbá.

items.spanish: Después de leer el texto k'iche', el fraile escribió una traducción.
items.english: After reading the K'iche' text, the friar wrote a translation.

items.spanish: Antes de sembrar, muchas familias hacen una ceremonia.
items.english: Before planting, many families hold a ceremony.

items.spanish: Cuando termine la cosecha, la familia celebrará una fiesta.
items.english: When the harvest is over, the family will hold a celebration.

sections.content: *Antes de* and *después de* are followed by the infinitive, never by a conjugated verb: *antes de crear*, not *antes de crearon*. If a different person does the second action, use *cuando* instead (*cuando llegue la lluvia*) or two sentences.
